selected.title: 'We've heard the feedback': TasWater rethinks big sewerage bill increases
selected.summary: Tasmanian businesses and sport clubs had said they were hit hard by the changes to sewerage prices, with one business stating their bill had risen from $630 to $3,800 a month.
selected.why: Utility policy reversal rethinking massive price increases following commercial feedback.
selected.fullText: TasWater to rethink sewerage pricing for businesses and sports clubs after big bill increases - ABC News Skip to main content Skip to news navigation, settings and search Explore the ABC news iview listen Loading ABC News News Home TasWater to rethink sewerage pricing for businesses and sports clubs after big bill increases Share Share article TasWater to rethink sewerage pricing for businesses and sports clubs after big bill increases Topic: Water Supply Posted Fri 2 Oct 2026 at 9:50am Fri 2 Oct 2026 at 9:50am Fri 2 Oct 2026 at 9:50am , updated Fri 2 Oct 2026 at 1:26pm Fri 2 Oct 2026 at 1:26pm Fri 2 Oct 2026 at 1:26pm TasWater says it will rectify the issue that saw some customers facing massive price increases. ( ABC News: Luke Bowden ) In short: TasWater will fix a recent sewerage pricing change that created massive price increases for some non-residential customers. The water utility had started charging a fixed sewerage cost based on the size of the water connection, but now acknowledges some customers weren't placing a high demand on the system. What's next? The changes will be backdated to July 1 and refunds issued for those who have paid. abc.net.au/news/taswater-agrees-to-rethink-price-increases-sewerage/107219744 Link copied Share Share article Tasmania's water utility is "assessing" changes to fixed sewerage charges that saw some non-residential customers facing a 500 per cent price increase. TasWater said a number of businesses and community groups, such as manufacturers and sporting clubs, had been affected, and it would make changes to lessen the impact. Under changes that came in from July 1, TasWater's fixed sewerage charges were based on the size of a property's water pipe connection, not their sewerage usage. "We've heard the feedback from this specific customer group, and we need to own and reflect on that while taking action to rectify the issue," TasWater general manager Callan Paske said in a statement. "While our charging methodology has resulted in lower charges for many customers, the transition has had unintended consequences for a number of customers whose large water connections do not reflect the comparatively low demand they place on the sewerage system." Sporting clubs reported massive price hikes due to the changes. ( ABC News: Georgia Hogge ) The price rises for water usage, including for households, are not affected by today's announcement. The economic regulator knocked back TasWater's request to rise water prices by 8.8 per cent over four years. Inst

reason: Australian utility pricing reveals tension between cost-recovery and cross-subsidy fairness that generalizes beyond water.
angle: Fixed-charge pricing based on connection size rather than usage is economically rational but politically untenable when it unmasks hidden subsidies.
